decisions.reason: Report locates the short name greet in dsh-plugin.naming.json pluginNames, distinguishes it from the coordinate acme/greet and package dsh-greet, and explicitly classifies it as a collision recommendation rather than a compatibility error, keeping the manifest loadable; prefixing is advised but not treated as mandatory.

Report locates the unprefixed service search, explains the collision/confusion risk with core and other plugins' services, and classifies it as a recommendation/warning rather than a compatibility error (noting the policy could not be verified to make it fatal); no strict-mode exit is misused as proof of incompatibility.

Report locates web-search/ready, treats it as informational pending registry context, and correctly avoids declaring a conflict from name overlap alone (could be a shared/standard channel). However, it never mentions publisher schema compatibility as a conflict determiner, covering only the registry-context half of the requirement.

Table covers every remaining declared surface (loader, tool, command, skill, skill provider, settings namespace, route, npm name). The report explicitly separates local manifest-level compatibility from unqueried registry occupancy, marks all availability questions unknown/not checked, proposes later registry verification without claiming it was run, does not invent an error from private:true, and explicitly rejects reserved/globally-available/all-clear claims.

caps.reason: The report draws no blanket all-clear conclusion: it reports zero compatibility errors but explicitly states no registry was queried, denies that any name is reserved or globally available, and lists unknown registry-dependent checks with proposed later verification.
